doc.title: Roy Haynes — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Buying the Oldsmobile convertible in 1950
summary: He parked a late-1949 Oldsmobile 98 outside Café Society, where Chan Parker mistook it for a Cadillac.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Yeah, we’re rolling. I want to talk about your car, because you’re making money to buy a car. Not everyone’s buying a car.
Then. Yeah, it was amazing then. It was then. You could count the drummers. Car. I had a convertible with the top down.
Describe it for us. What brand, etc.? And how much did you pay for it?

It was a 19 . . . – a late – what was it? I bought it in 1950. So it was a late ’49 98 convertible Oldsmobile, light gray. I remember having it parked in front of Café Society. The hood was as long as this room then. It was when they had the last of the rocket engines. The top was down. I was coming out of Café Society with Bird and Chan. Chan was young and beautiful then. Chan says to Bird, “Bird, is that a Cadillac?” And Bird says, “Yes.” It was an Oldsmobile. But oh man, it was so beautiful. Not only the car, but just – but I had money before I went with Bird. It wasn’t – people say, “How you playing with Bird and buying a new car?”
